HOW TO USE THE ROUNDS
- Rounds 1 and 2 are not counted. Only the round 3 final bid decides the award. You can use rounds 1 and 2 to test positions and read the platform's replies.
- Round 1: test a 4-week, tier 4 bid at a price that clears your own cost at that tier with a margin. This tests whether the quality step is affordable and competitive. If your own cost at tier 4 is not known, price it at your cost plus a modest margin.
- Round 2: if the reply says you are close or ahead, hold price and terms, or make only a small move. If it says you are far behind, consider the other delivery and quality options, but still keep your price at or above your own cost.
- Round 3: submit the final bid. Choose the terms that maximise (price minus your cost) times your estimated chance of winning. Do not drop price just because the platform suggests it. Only cut price if your own cost data says the lower bid still makes a profit.

RECOMMENDED STANCE
Prioritise a positive margin over winning at any cost. Test quality in round 1 at 4 weeks, tier 4 if your own cost allows it. Use round 2 to decide between holding and a small move. For round 3, submit the highest-profit bid your own cost data supports, and do not go below your own cost at the chosen terms.
